# HAX at Penn State

> HAX is Penn State's free, open-source website builder. Students, faculty and staff can publish accessible course sites, portfolios and project sites with no coding required.

This is the full text of the hax.psu.edu homepage as Markdown, for AI assistants and other clients that do not run JavaScript. Canonical page: https://hax.psu.edu/. A shorter link map is at https://hax.psu.edu/llms.txt.

## Quick links

## What is HAX?

**A standards-based publishing platform for *web authoring* and *content ownership*.**

HAX is Penn State's open-source web authoring platform for accessible, standards-based publishing. It helps teams publish faster without sacrificing quality through portable content and long-term ownership not tied to a single vendor.

HAX supports teaching, research, outreach, and student development with a shared platform that scales from one course site to institution-wide initiatives.

### Part of Penn State?

[Log in to get started](https://hax.psu.edu/login.php)

#### Prefer command line?

```
npm install --global @haxtheweb/create
hax start
```

## Built for every role at Penn State

**Faculty** - Create and update accessible course materials quickly. Reuse content across semesters, keep ownership of your work, and focus on teaching instead of platform complexity.

**Focus on teaching**, *not complexity!*

**Students** - Build portfolios, resumes, and project sites you can take with you beyond graduation. HAX is portable and lightweight, and it gives students meaningful ways to learn by doing while contributing to a vibrant campus publishing community.

**Staff** - Build a department website, a project website, or a personal website for a short-term initiative, anything you need. Set up a quick site to talk about a project, download the site and host it on another server. Host content from github or anywhere else. HAX is there to help you get your job done faster with less training.

## Institutional impact

HAX combines academic flexibility with operational discipline. It is supported through cross-college collaboration and designed for long-term maintainability.

- Open-source and portable architecture that reduces vendor lock-in risk
- Accessibility-forward publishing practices
- Shared governance across participating units
- Demonstrated adoption across courses, programs, and public-facing sites

[Discuss adoption for your unit](mailto:bmr1@psu.edu)

## About

HAX is a service provided through a collaboration between [Penn State College of Arts and Architecture](https://arts.psu.edu/), [College of Information Sciences and Technology](https://ist.psu.edu/), [College of Education](https://ed.psu.edu/), [**Eberly College of Science**](https://science.psu.edu/), and [**University Libraries**](https://libraries.psu.edu/). The platform is powered by *HAXcms*, originally developed to power 100s of high scale online courses.

### Interested in collaboration?

Contact [Bill Rose, Product Owner](mailto:bmr1@psu.edu).

## Privacy policy

Penn State IT does not monitor websites and does not assume responsibility for any published content. The content authors are responsible for the content of their websites. Use of this service is governed by [Penn State policies and guidelines](https://security.psu.edu/awareness/psu-policies/), including [Penn State IT Web Services Policy](https://policy.psu.edu/policies/ad54). All pages must be compliant with [Accessibility Standards, Policy AD69](https://policies.psu.edu/policies/ad69).

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Who can use HAX?

Anyone, anywhere! Thanks to HAX being open source, all you need is a web server and a domain name to get started. We also support publishing directly to GitHub pages and other static publishing tools for advanced developer use-cases. If you are part of Penn State though you can just click [log in](https://hax.psu.edu/login.php) to get started immediately!

### Who supports HAX?

The HAX user community is supported internal to Penn State by a collaboration between several units including the College of Arts and Architecture, College of Information Sciences and Technology, College of Education, Eberly College of Science, and University Libraries. HAX also receives contributions from groups outside of Penn State including Buttercups LLC and community members at large.

### How do I join the community?

Join our community Discord channel to get support from the community and the HAX team. [Join the HAX Discord](https://discord.gg/aCGxmRHEJP)

### Why was HAX created?

HAX is a response to a lack of products existing to meet the needs of producing accessible and engaging web content in online course environments. The university has a rich history of building a mix of custom, open source and buying repurposed commercial products with varying success.

HAX was born out of a university Request For Information (RFI) that sought to build a custom Drupal Instructional Content management System (iCMS). After requirements were gathered by stakeholders across the university, it was determined that the best path forward was to build a new kind of solution as the system requirements described were far beyond what any commercial product was offering, and no vendors responded to the Request for proposal after initial RFI process.

### How are decisions made?

Decisions about the platform are influenced by a mix of needs from students, faculty and staff either taking courses delivered via the platform or actively building material with the platform. The direction of HAX is steered by the *Core Product Development team* which meets monthly and is made up of representatives from any group contributing development, design, or other skillsets toward the platform's development and sustainment. If you would like to join the *Core Product Development team* please contact [Bill Rose, Product Owner](mailto:bmr1@psu.edu).

### What's with the 8-bit RPG characters?

Our 8-bit vibe was a design challenge presented to four College of IST students in the Spring of 2022. They were tasked with creating an over-world design that was fun, inviting, creative, and unique. The team took these requirements and built an experience that is playful, easy to use, and feels more like playing a video game than building a website. This inspired the creation of future iterations of the system which get more professional with each release, yet still retain the playful aspects at times to remind us of who we are building for.

Much like 8-bit video games were designed to be approachable and fun for all ages, HAX is designed to be approachable and fun for all skill levels! Each RPG style character is unique to the user logging in and helps provide a humanizing touch. Websites produced by HAX can be a mix of professional and playful but the 8-bit design helps you designate between the admin task and what end-users see.
